summary: Wisconsin fire tower built at Pembine in 1933 or 1934; sold as surplus in 1990, moved to Paust's resort, now in Governor Thompson State Park; the Pembine site is listed as gone.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower (NHLR); wall material metal and International Stacey Company named in the architect field (Wisconsin Historical Society)
facts.status_note: The original tower at Pembine is listed as gone; the same tower stands in Governor Thompson State Park as the Paust tower (FFLA, NHLR)

staffing.status: Active lookout until the 1980s (Historical Society); the Register says it served until the 1980s; no lookout names found in the sources read

facts.agency: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (current administrator, per NHLR)

access.note: The Paust tower is listed in Governor Thompson State Park (NHLR). No source says whether the tower itself can be climbed or viewed up close.

events.note: Built at its original location in T37N, R20E, Sec. 36 in November 1933 (Historical Society). The Register gives 1934 and credits the Civilian Conservation Corps
A November 12, 1936 newspaper item, quoted on the Faithorn page, reports a telephone line being run from the Wisconsin fire tower near Pembine to the Michigan tower at Faithorn
State declared the tower surplus and sold it to Dale Paust
Moved by Dale Paust to his Woods Lake resort, per the Historical Society; the Register says he moved and rebuilt it there without a date
State purchased the Paust Woods Lake Resort for a state park
Governor Thompson State Park opened, per Wikipedia

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Historical Society gives November 1933 at the original location and does not name the CCC. The Register gives 1934 and credits the CCC. Both dates are recorded; the story says the sources differ and that only the Register names the CCC.

The Register calls it an Aermotor tower; the Historical Society names International Stacey Company in its architect field. The sources do not explain how the two fit together, so both are reported without a choice.
The Historical Society dates the move to 1991. The Register dates the sale to 1990 and says the move happened without a date.
The FFLA lists the original Pembine tower as gone and the Paust tower as standing. The record's relocated status fits the original site; the story covers both places.

notes_for_editor: The record coordinates (45.63292, -87.95457) match the FFLA Pembine entry marked Tower Gone, so the record is the original site. The Paust tower sits far southwest of Pembine, at about 45.33, -88.22 per FFLA and NHLR. The build year (1933 vs 1934) and the Stacey/Aermotor question are not resolved. No lookout names or specific fires were found. One WebSearch added nothing beyond the FFLA county list and the NHLR page. The existing us-wi-pembine-at-paust story covers the same tower from the Paust end; this record covers the original site. The OSM elevation (332 m) in the brief was not checked. No photos added.
